record.paper_title: Open Problems in Data-Sharing Peer-to-Peer Systems
record.original_question: What are the effects of denial-of-service attacks other than query-flood attacks across different peer-to-peer network designs, and what defenses are effective against those attacks in practice?

evidence.quote: However, more research is necessary to understand the effects of other types of DoS attacks in various P2P networks.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad open research direction concerning DoS attacks beyond query-flooding in P2P systems and the defenses against them. While there is an extensive body of work on specific sub-problems (Sybil-resistant identity protocols, Eclipse-attack defenses in DHTs such as Kademlia, churn modeling, P2P-based amplification attacks), no comprehensive, design-by-design characterization with matching defenses and provable guarantees exists. The problem remains an open research program rather than a single resolved theorem.

status_evidence.title: Survey of DHT security techniques
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys defenses against Sybil, Eclipse, and routing attacks in structured P2P overlays and notes many remaining open questions.
status_evidence.claim: Comprehensive provable defenses across all P2P designs are not established.

status_evidence.title: Amplification attacks via P2P networks
status_evidence.snippet: Studies show P2P protocols can be abused for DRDoS amplification, with mitigations still evolving.
status_evidence.claim: Non-flood DoS vectors in P2P remain an active research area.
